points.description: States that the wireframe representation is ambiguous: a single wireframe model can be interpreted as, or represent, more than one different solid object (e.g. the same edges/vertices can be read as different solids).
points.partial_credit: 0.75 if only 'ambiguous' / 'unclear representation' is stated without saying one model can represent different solid objects (or vice versa).

points.description: States the consequence that the wireframe model becomes messy and confusing (cluttered with edges, hard to interpret visually).

rubric.notes: Only one limitation is asked for, and the model answer's limitation is ambiguity: one wireframe can stand for several different solids. Full marks need both the ambiguity idea stated precisely (P1) and the messy/confusing result (P2). A vague or other limitation (e.g. no surface or volume data, no hidden line removal) is not in the model answer and earns nothing; any wrong statement about the point voids it.
